contract: Bounded local durable-Unit identity admission, serialized route processing barriers and idle sleep/wake over caller-owned OTP Registry and DynamicSupervisor, preserving the Unit's transient restart and shutdown policy.
limits: Finite DY1–DY7 lifecycle/race scenarios using volatile Memory, not universal recovery, disk durability or exactly-once delivery proofs.
Registry uniqueness is local; distinct registries do not exclude each other. Store CAS, not this directory, arbitrates uncoordinated contenders.
Mailbox delivery is volatile; routed means a normally completed processing barrier, not application acceptance. Barrier exit is indeterminate with no resend. Caller timeout is uncertain.
Idle counts directory start/route operations, not direct Unit intake, outbox work or external async activity. Slow operations block the directory; no exact wall-clock or throughput guarantee.
Caller owns one fresh jointly supervised infrastructure subtree after loss, a dedicated positive finite supervisor cap and matching deterministic per-stream Unit options; no orphan adoption.
Bookkeeping excludes mailbox backlog, durable Store history and application state. Sleep does not cancel actions, checkpoint, delete data or prove an external Effect did not run.
No durable mailbox/directory, cluster lease, arbitrary child framework, retry scheduler, hot configuration or new business-state policy. Inherited OTP diagnostics remain caller Logger policy.

grounding.claim: Named DY1–DY7 finite scenarios cover identity/validation, routing/death/stop/expiry barriers, supervisor capacity, abnormal recovery/named shutdown/intensity, sleep and idle refresh, Store CAS contention and bounded binary lifecycle/infrastructure reset; no universal or distributed correctness proof.
Pinned GenServer, unique-key Registry, DynamicSupervisor capacity/termination and ordinary Supervisor lifecycle contracts.
OTP 29.1.2 same-sender ordering, monitors, monotonic timers and transient restart/intensity contracts are relied on, not locally proved.

Caller supplies and jointly resets a dedicated bounded local infrastructure subtree, one identity-domain namespace, matching deterministic Unit options, and all ready DurableUnit Store/transition/dispatcher Needs. Assembly owns business orchestration and late-outcome policy.

telemetry.contract: No new telemetry events or payload logs. Inherited OTP diagnostics remain caller Logger policy.

config.contract: Required caller-owned named unique Registry, dedicated local DynamicSupervisor, arity-1 unit_options and idle_ms integer 1..4_294_967_295 milliseconds; optional ordinary OTP name. Supervisor owns the positive finite max_children cap; fixed at construction, no hot changes.

control.contract: start admits or finds an owned child; stop confirms termination/spec removal or absence; route validates and sends the unchanged durable_unit_input tuple followed by a same-controller snapshot barrier. Explicit pre-send errors, routed on normal barrier return, indeterminate delivery on exit; find inspects without idle refresh. No drain or external-action cancellation.
